description: Remote Sensing Engineer, with experience in various fields but a passion for space. I believe this challenge to be the most interesting and flexible, giving the most freedom to mabipulate the data and create something original
summary: Python-based script and GUI which allows anyone to import NASA EIC media and convert them to a custom sound track, thanks to a main brightness-to-frequency conversion and secondary tracks generation based on selectable metrics, and can single audio stems for further processing using an external mixing software
details: Python tool with custom interface that can convert to audio track any image or video file based on its visual characteristics. From pictures, every column of pixel is extracted and generates a sound (50 columns per 1 second of audio are sampled), and the same happen on video frames, where a column can be extracted in the same spot of different time frames or sweeping both in the time and horizontal frame dimension. This allows to have the same output wether an image or video is processed, which is a matrix of all the extracted columns arranged with the audio time axis as horizontal axis. The matrix obtained can then be filtered (according to user settings) to remove rapid changes and brightness fluctuations that would be reflected in sharp sound changes. Finally, the main audio track is obtained by mapping, for every extracted column, the pixel height to sound frequency and the pixel brightness to sound amplitude. Additionally, different pixel colors can be associated to different timbre filters applied to describe the image colors using their variation. in this way, using for example a sweep left to right on an image, loud high tones are associated with something bright in the top of the picture along the sweep, hearable low tones would indicate that the bottom region has now become brighter, and the sound timbre will identify the color as well: this allows for a full image spatial characterization, where the audio time is associated with the column sweep direction (always horizontal) and the sound frequency with the vertical direction: with few simple instructions, this would allow for someone incapable of seeing to reconstruct the color and brightness distribution of the image, while the secondary tracks that are generated as well (derived from multiple image parameters in the currently scanned region: pixel column contrast, saturation and spot brightness location, ...) can be associated to other sounds that can reconstruct the image feeling. This interface was then built to make the sonification process highly customizable, both during the process and after using external tools, so that the amount and quality of the sound obtained can be tailored to the user's needs and is not restricted by our teams' skills and ability with audio mixing, but can instead be used by the widest audience possible for entertainement and accessibility purposes
